dominant_breach: rental pricing software can convert dispersed landlords into a coordinated data-and-recommendation system that raises rents or suppresses independent price competition while renters lack usable visibility into the coordination channel
fastest_washout: nonpublic competitor data, rent-recommendation adoption pressure, algorithmic sameness, lease-renewal timing, and high moving costs wash out household bargaining before antitrust remedies arrive

rental_market_power_gate.note: Rental market power must be scored directly where pricing tools pool competitor information or align recommendations that affect ordinary rent payments.

algorithmic_rent_setting_coordination.note: The RealPage docket and response-to-comments record make algorithmic rent-setting a live antitrust/remedy case: competitor data flows, pricing recommendations, and compliance monitoring must be proven, not assumed.

competitor_data_pooling_in_pricing_tools.note: Active scoring turns on whether competitively sensitive landlord data are pooled, shared, aged, aggregated, firewalled, or used to align rent decisions.

rent_recommendation_adoption_monitoring.note: Certification requires audit evidence on adoption rates, override behavior, recommendation identity/similarity, and whether price-decrease features are chilled.

landlord_pricing_independence_audit.note: A proposed judgment or settlement posture is not enough; the cube needs monitoring evidence that landlords retain independent pricing and that tenants receive practical restoration where inflated rent occurred. Rev0344 unused-source burn-down: OECD market-dynamism evidence is now bound as context for competition/coordination risk.

housing_land_washout.note: Rent increases wash out lower-half wealth by converting income gains into landlord revenue before savings can accumulate.

household_market_extraction_gate.note: Recurring rent is a household tollgate; coordinated pricing is scored as extraction when renters cannot avoid or remedy the channel.

measurement_uncertainty_band.note: The cube needs a data-room standard for tenant incidence, market coverage, and tool adoption, not only allegations or settlement terms.

housing_market_power_remedy_access.note: Antitrust remedies must be tested against renter relief, monitoring, data deletion/firewalls, and whether the harm is restored at household level.

proof_debt: tenant-level rent incidence and overcharge estimates by income, race, household type, and market
market-level coverage of rental pricing software and competitor-data ingestion
adoption and override rates for rent recommendations
tenant refund/restoration pathways after antitrust remedy
independent-pricing audit logs and monitor reports

gate_05_washout_reconcentration.why: Coordinated rent pricing can wash out household gains through recurring rent extraction before asset formation occurs.

gate_06_wealth_to_rule_capture.why: Landlord/software coordination can convert data control and market concentration into rent-rule power.

gate_10_measurement_uncertainty_owner_vi.why: The key facts are tool coverage, data lineage, adoption, override, and tenant incidence, all of which require structured evidence access.

gate_11_enforceability_remedies_capture_.why: Conduct remedies need monitoring and household restoration tests, not only prospective software restrictions.

gate_15_place_public_finance_service_wea.why: Rental-market coordination is place-specific; local market share and tightness decide whether renters can exit.

gate_16_household_market_extraction_cost.why: Rent is the largest recurring household cost for many renters; coordinated price setting is a direct wealth-washout mechanism.

gate_17_score_mediated_exclusion_algorit.why: Algorithmic recommendations become wealth-relevant when they are opaque, hard to contest, and applied at lease-renewal thresholds.
